title: Pages — the shell, round 2: the pin, the welcome words, two fuller sample pages

steps.path: Top bar → Pages, the top-right corner of each card
steps.headline: The pin on each card is now an upright push-pin, filled in when the page is pinned.
steps.changed: The tilted pin from round 1 ("looks a little odd") is replaced by the familiar upright pin, drawn a little larger.
steps.notice: Pinned pages show a solid pin; unpinned pages show an outline. Hover still says Pin or Unpin.

steps.path: Top bar → Pages, before you have any
steps.headline: The welcome card now names pages worth wanting: a calendar, a news feed, an email browser, a team timesheet.
steps.changed: The two example sentences were rewritten from your round-1 note. Everything else on the card is unchanged.
steps.notice: The first thing a new person reads suggests something bigger than a timer.
steps.risk: Those examples need connections, which arrive in Phase 2; the words promise the destination, not the first release.

steps.headline: Week planner replaces the notes board: seven day columns, events by kind, done or to do, and a quick add.
steps.changed: A fuller sample page. Today's column is marked, events carry a colour by kind, clicking one marks it done, Add event opens a small form, and the bar underneath counts the week.
steps.notice: This is the kind of page the creator should aim for, built only from the page style kit.
steps.risk: It is a sample with made-up events; the real calendar page comes with Phase 2's connections.

steps.path: Top bar → the Paint studio pinned button
steps.headline: Paint studio replaces the bare canvas: tools on the left, a palette and brush settings on the right, undo and redo.
steps.changed: Brush, eraser, line, rectangle and ellipse; twelve colours plus a custom one; size and opacity with a live preview; undo, redo, clear; keyboard shortcuts. The paper stays white in every theme.
steps.notice: The studio's frame follows the theme; the painting does not. That is the rule for pictures and art.
steps.risk: Save as picture only shows Saved for now; a page cannot write a file until Phase 3.

steps.path: The thin header above an open page
steps.headline: You may want to revisit the page header. What would you change?
steps.today: An open page shows a thin header: its name and where it lives on the left; Pin, Edit in chat and Esc · Back on the right.
steps.problem: In round 1 you said you may want to come back to this layout, without saying what felt off.
steps.proposal: Tell me what to change, or leave it as it is for now and revisit once real pages exist.
steps.prompt: For example: hide the header while a page is open, move Edit in chat, show the page's icon larger…
